To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the singularities of the pentapods with base attachments coplanar to each other and with a fixed base are the same that the ones of the classical Stewart platform, but the singularities of pentapods with non-coplanar base attachments are different.
the singularity analysis for pentapod manipulators is completed, and that a measure of distance from architectural singularities is provided.

(1) the singularity locus is a 3-dimensional surface in the 5-dimensional space of leg lengths; (2) the surface is formed by 5 branches, each of which contains a 2-dimensional curve that is an architectural singularity; (3) the distance of a point of the surface to an architectural singularity is the shortest distance between the point and the 5 curves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the singularities of pentapods, with the aim of obtaining a better insight on their geometric structure.
the study of the architectural singularities in a particular class of pentapod manipulators, with the purpose of obtaining an optimal design of such manipulators.
the study of architectural singularities of pentapods, with coplanar leg attachments, in order to improve the design process of this class of fully parallel manipulators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the architectural singularities of the pentapods studied here are not only algebraically characterized, but also geometrically interpreted and located in the workspace.

the architectural singularities of a pentapod with coplanar attachments are located at the intersections between the singularity locus (which is a quartic algebraic curve in the workspace of the manipulator), and the plane containing the base attachments.
architectural singularities are not to be considered a problem but a resource in pentapod design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the location of the legs in the base of a pentapod can be used to obtain manipulators with good global behavior and with a high inclination capability in the tool axis.

, in the case of pentapods with a coplanar base, the architectural singularities are not only a consequence of the particular geometry of the legs, but they are also related to the location of the base attachments.

we have provided a complete characterization for architectural singularities in pentapods with planar base attachments, including the algebraic conditions for their existence and a geometrical description of them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the architecture of the manipulator has a deep impact on the global behavior of the system, and thus, a proper design of such architecture should be considered as a first step in the design process.
, for a given pentapod with coplanar legs, the location of the legs in the base plane is a key parameter to control the distance to architectural singularites.
architectural singularities are closely related to the geometry of the base of the manipulator, and that their number and location can be controlled by means of leg rearrangements.
